system.summary: Saxon system S1 of Wackerbarth's Vienna mission (March-June 1717): homophonic substitution of French letters in 1-2 digit numbers (e 2/10, i 9, o 16/22/33, t 28/52 ...), polygrams and a nomenclator in 3-digit numbers (154 Votre Excellence, 177 le Czar, 217 le roi d'Angleterre, 252 le roi de Prusse, 292 la Pologne, 355 premier), 4-digit nulls (50xx and others), clear words interspersed. The volume's Nov.-Dec. 1717 letters use another system, S2 = the Flemming key K0 of Loc. 00675/10.
system.notes: S1 is not the Flemming key K0 (Loc. 00675/10, view 0080), nor its shifted variant, nor Wackerbarth's 1703 key. A.-S. Rous (The Keys of Diplomacy) describes the 1717 system as substitution in 1-3 digit numbers, mostly 2, with 355 and 1000 in the nomenclator.

prior_solution.where: Many S1 passages of the volume carry interlinear decipherments of the time (the key was rebuilt from them); the letter of 24 April 1717 has a full decipherment sheet of the time (ff. 33-33v). Relation XXII has none. A.-S. Rous (The Keys of Diplomacy, University of Tartu repository) works on this corpus and lists the 1717 letter as not deciphered.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocols hashed before each single measurement; a partial reading may be published if explained); on 11 Nov 2026, after the second measurement, he decided to accept the held-out language test alone as the condition for reading Relation XXII (post hoc, declared). Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, built the key, wrote and ran the protocols, read and wrote up. No human read the reading against the scans. For the letter of 20 Oct. 1715 he answered once a blind plate of digit shapes (W1, two controls passed) and approved adding the letter to this target.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, key, protocols, measurements, reading, write-up)

solution.what: Glossed S1 views (training) and their glosses, Relation XXII views 0089-0099 and the letter of 24 April 1717 (views 0037-0040) transcribed, each part hashed before decoding; the decipherment sheet of the time 0042-0043 transcribed.
Key rebuilt by aligning cipher groups on the interlinear decipherments of the time of the glossed S1 views (keys KEY-W1717, then b and c by a mechanical rule written beforehand).

Protocol 1 (hashed): test A (view 0040 vs the sheet of the time) 0.204 vs 0.086 for 200 permuted keys, under threshold; test B (lexical cover, 360 groups of Rel. XXII) 0.9375 vs 0.9231. Both failed; instrument at fault (diagnosed afterwards).

Protocol 2 (hashed): A' ground truth (letter of 28 May 1717 held out) 0.339 exact vs max 0.128, margin 0.21 < 0.30: failed. B' held-out language test (view 0091, 353 groups, criterion L7 calibrated on training): z = 11.5, gap 0.74: passed. The protocol's rule required both.

Under Avenant 3 (post hoc: B' alone accepted, 95% as final check), Relation XXII read by sense with frozen key c: 716 cipher words, 575 certain, 66 probable, 66 restored, 9 unresolved = 89.5%. A variant counting nine recurring homophones absent from c (about 97.9%) is not adopted. Letter of 24 April read against its sheet (not blind): 90.8%.

Letter of 20 Oct. 1715: key K1715 learnt only from the glossed views 0388-0390 of Loc. 00712/05 (majority vote, 57 numbers, 934 pairs), frozen before the measurement; same system as S1 of 1717 (47/50 common numbers agree).

Pre-registered single measurement (PREREG-1715) on the blind control portion view 0384 left (307 groups): S = 0.945 vs max of 400 witness keys 0.730, rank 1/401, threshold 0.77 calibrated on training only: passed.

Letter of 20 Oct. 1715 read by sense with K1715, completed by S1/1717 values and context (counted probable); blind plate W1 of nine digit shapes answered by Brice Dudout (controls 2/2), three words made certain: 922 cipher words, 774 certain, 118 probable, 12 restored, 18 unresolved = 96.75%.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the interlinear decipherments of the time on other letters of the same volume and system (S1), then applied to Relation XXII, which has no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md, Relation XXII cipher words: 575 certain + 66 probable = 641 of 716 = 89.5% (frozen/scripts/compte_lecture.py); 66 restored not counted (98.7% with them).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered tests, not docs/_validate.py. Held-out language test B' passed (view 0091, z = 11.54, gap 0.742, criterion L7 calibrated on training only); the ground-truth test A' FAILED (0.339 vs 0.128, margin 0.21 < 0.30) and the protocol required both. Accepting B' alone was decided after the measurement (Avenant 3, SHA-256 7b0ee565...c151). A first protocol (tests A and B) also failed. Hence 'weak', not 'pass'. Letter of 20 Oct. 1715 (s15_validation.txt): its own pre-registered measurement PASSED (S 0.945 vs 0.730, rank 1/401, theta 0.77); the verdict above stays 'weak' for key c of 1717.

credits.note: simultaneous work: Anne-Simone Rous (The Keys of Diplomacy, University of Tartu repository) works on the Wackerbarth-Flemming cipher correspondence 1700-1720; she describes the structure of the 1717 system of Loc. 00713/01 (1-3 digit numbers, 355 and 1000 in the nomenclator), lists the 1717 letter as not deciphered, and reports a glossed simple substitution in 1715; she may have read the letter of 20 Oct. 1715 (Loc. 00712/05). Our readings were made independently and are to be cited with her work.

texts.label: Relation XXII, Wackerbarth to Augustus II, Vienna 14-16 June 1717
texts.summary: Chancellor Sinzendorf, by order of Charles VI, proposes to Wackerbarth (and the day before to Saint-Saphorin) a concert of the Emperor, the King of Poland and the King of England to restore the tranquillity of the Empire and an entire peace in the North on a just balance, possibly a triple alliance; the stay of the Russians in the Empire is referred to the Diet of Ratisbon and the directors of the Circles; George I wants the same measures regarding Poland and nothing returned to the King of Sweden; strict secrecy.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout
reading_review.note: Read as French sentences of 1717 against decryption.txt: the cipher words construe with the clear words around them over the whole letter, and the translation follows; but 66 words are restored (numbers absent from the key), 9 unresolved and 66 only probable, so 89.5%: grade B, read in part. The condition for reading was decided after the measurement (A' failed). AI agents only; no human read the reading; not re-checked blind on the images.

texts.label: Wackerbarth to Flemming, Vienna 24 April 1717 (checked against the decipherment of the time)
texts.summary: The King of Sweden's designs on Poland (a landing near Danzig); the fear that Sweden may detach the Czar from the Northern League, which Vienna should thwart; the Hanau exchange: the Electors' consents must be won directly, not through the Emperor (promise of Ferdinand II to John George I); request for full power and a draft treaty.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout
reading_review.note: Key c reads 188/207 cipher words of views 0037-0039 as French sentences agreeing in sense with the decipherment sheet of the time (ff. 33-33v), which renders the whole letter; 7 unresolved nomenclator codes are resolved by the sheet. Not blind: the sheet had been transcribed before. The translation follows the sheet. Grade B.

texts.label: Wackerbarth (camp before Stralsund) to his wife in Vienna, 20 October 1715, copy
texts.summary: Answering a 'reasoning' put to the countess at the imperial court, Wackerbarth says that Charles XII will be driven from the Empire (Stralsund closely besieged, Wismar blockaded since Poel was taken); Augustus II wants a general peace, not a separate one, and no total ruin of Sweden; the remnants that might carry Charles XII back to Poland should be destroyed now; he will write to General Dücker and ask Count Virmond to come, so that peace may be made under the Emperor's mediation.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout; digit shapes of nine words checked by Brice Dudout (blind plate W1)
reading_review.note: Read as French sentences of 1715 against s15_decryption.txt: the cipher words construe with the clear text around them over the whole letter, and the translation follows; 96.75% by Daniel's rule. Grade B, not A: the certain/probable classification was made by a single reader; 72 = ch and 96 = le are only probable; 12 restored and 18 unresolved words. Brice Dudout's blind plate checked only nine digit shapes (controls 2/2).

outcome.notes: New partial reading of Relation XXII, which has no decipherment of the time; to be cited as simultaneous work with A.-S. Rous. The letter of 24 April 1717, listed by Rous as not deciphered, is rendered in full by the sheet of the time at ff. 33-33v. key.tsv section A = frozen key c (CC BY 4.0); section B = proposals after the measurement, not counted. No image or derivative of the Dresden scans (In Copyright) is included. The letter of 20 Oct. 1715 (Loc. 00712/05) uses the same system S1; its key K1715 (s15_key.tsv, CC BY 4.0) was learnt from glosses in its own volume; it is 'read' (96.75%), while the target stays 'read in part' because of Relation XXII.
